# the contributor audit: retained cap geometry, a roof action, and scale selection

## 1. Joint cap and selector compactification

Full read of `candidate 714f69e684c396b1`: PASS with its fixed group/contact and common-test scopes. the contributor reran 112 exact checks; Two-sided also independently audited the complete source.

The minimum-norm finite threshold clamp is used only as an auxiliary record.
It preserves every proper or supporting trace exactly and retains strict
full/empty statuses. It is not substituted into the old projected cover.
The joint product domination survives weak convergence. Passing the local
Gauss--Green identity then determines limiting section allocations, including
inside complement and outside equality. This rules out hidden edge atoms in
the section measure; it does not impose the old inside-zero convention after
a proper section becomes supporting.

The surviving groups have a common allocated section mean equal to the
kappa-weighted contact barycenter, with balanced continuous normals. They
cover the continuous planes at their retained contact bases. A full cover
after discarding zero-weight groups and a base-normal resultant remain
unclaimed. The ordinary physical stress follows for common bounded tested
speeds from total-variation removal of the correction terms.

## 2. Paired roofs give a genuine geometric exclusion

Full read of `candidate fed95f84ea97787a`: PASS. the contributor reran the inherited 1,529 checks and 1,587 new exact checks.

The finite affine roof-plane motion is an actual compatible body motion. Its
generally nonconvex boundary speed is recovered by bounded decreasing convex
penalties, so a finite penalty is chosen before passing to the buffer limit.
On every moving prism, strict crossing makes the two paired roof indicators
sum to one. Thus the response is exactly (1/2-beta) times the removed mass.
The cap-law extension follows by Tonelli and needs no finite critical-menu
selection. Atomic weights retain their explicit roof-credit condition.

The zero-buffer rectangle calibration is a complete all-normal example with
an actual strict body descent: the two old caps continue to cover the source
fiber, their masses decrease by half the total removed mass, and the other
base gaps persist. No lower bound on the new maximum is needed to prove the
strict decrease. The theorem's crossing and available-roof hypotheses are
substantive and are not automatic for a general extremal family.

## 3. Scalar-penalized attainment and the same-force equation

Full read of `candidate 281b285239e28b38`: PASS under its standing compact bad-base framework and explicitly retained actual-response premises.

The trial epsilon=tau/C lies below a fixed bad sublevel for small tau. Since
epsilon_bar<1, the penalty is nonnegative, so every minimizing sequence also
lies in the required original sublevel. At fixed tau the scalar stays away
from zero. The existing parameter compactness proof works uniformly on this
positive scalar interval, and fixed-slice minimality permits the old positivity
and finite-plane package after attainment.

The two-sided linear gap gives explicit bounds epsilon/tau between 1/(eC)
and 2 log(2C/c)/c, making the scalar minimum interior for small tau. Extending
each actual path by epsilon(t)=epsilon exp(st) adds exactly -s delta_ia to
the contact budget. The objective's common improvement is M tau s, so one
separator tested against both scalar signs gives Delta=M tau. Body and
parameter tests at s=0 retain the old equations and the unpenalized beta.

No derivative of an optimized value is invoked. The source retains the
finite covering, actual continuation, addable-cone and uniform envelope
hypotheses needed for that separator. These hypotheses must not be omitted
when applying the result. A geometric Gamma payment is still absent.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
